feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Iteration 8 (mass 0.5 kg, 303.6) is the best design so far, and its oval finished 16 of 20 runs (mean finish 1.86 s) while the s-bend (line_loss 2.0) and slalom (line_loss 3.0) still went off track in all runs. Your choice to hold the geometry is supported. Iterations 4 to 8 show that span (iteration 5), footprint (iteration 6), track width at 0.10 m (iteration 7) and forward position (iterations 2 to 4) each either left bend line loss at 2.0 or cost oval finishes. Bend line loss is therefore most likely a control-response limit, which is why this iteration tests the controller only. Next race: if the s-bend or slalom line_loss_events falls below 2.0 or 3.0 with the controller change, hold the geometry and report which change did it. If the oval finish rate falls below 0.75 with no bend improvement, the geometry is not the cause and the controller should revert to the iteration-8 settings. If bend line loss is still 2.0 and 3.0 after the controller change, the geometry search should stop, as you planned.
requested_changes: Hold the iteration-8 geometry (x = plus or minus 0.025 m, y = 0.075 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.5 kg) for the controller test, so the controller result can be read cleanly.

If the bend line loss remains at 2.0 and 3.0 after the controller change, and the oval still finishes near 0.8, test one exploratory geometry change: wheel_track 0.14 m. The 0.10 m test (iteration 7) lost the oval finishes, so the wider track is the untested direction for bend stability.
Keep the five sensors at y = 0.075 m and the 50 mm span. Both have been the best-performing sensing layout, and widening the span or enlarging the footprint each cost oval finishes.
